Introduction
Justice week was planned to take place two weeks before spring break. Caution: this is
not to conflict with other “big weeks” (ex: Rez week, Earth Day, etc). Preparations for a
spring Justice Week need to begin in the fall; room reservations, partner organization
and church partnership contacts. Although some plans will need to be changed from
the master plan, use the Justice Week Toolkit at www.ijm.org to help plan the week.
Make sure to update this document following every Justice Week.
Goals
1. Awareness: For students and professors to become aware of the reality of injustice
in our world and equipped with tools to combating injustice.
2. Gospel Conversations: For people to learn about the God of justice – who is
present and active in our world today – through believers’ words and deeds.

Soularium Table- CSU justice week
“Thanks for your desire to help engage the CSU students and faculty on the topic
of justice. Enjoy your time as you are, for a moment, the voice of those who are
enslaved and oppressed around the world. Pray that God will use this hour to
raise up an army who will combat the evil in the world and become those who ‘set
the captives free’.”
The goals of the table:
To engage our community on the topic of injustice.
To raise awareness of the issue and catalyze help.
To represent the heart of Christ to the campus, as those with no voice are close
to His heart.
Please:
Use Soularium cards as a springboard into your conversation.
Replace the standard Soularium questions with the following:
a)
Which image best represents injustice? Why?
b)
Which image best represents justice? Why?
c)
Which image best represents God’s view of injustice? Why?
Listen well and limit your speaking.
Speak boldly of your hope in Christ and how He came to bring an end to
injustice.
Get contact information from those who visit the table.

Consumerism Day
• This day is intended to educate the campus on how the way they
consume affects modern day slavery.
• Set-up (how far in advance do you need to start and what needs to be
done?): Contacting Fair Trade companies to be involved. Start several
months before for both being on campus and for donations; many
companies need 6 weeks advance notice to make donations. Make sure to
“ok” coffee give-away with event planning (plaza) or the flea market desk
at least a month ahead of time.
• Find resources for how to shop slave-free and put together info for
people to take. Try Slaveryfootprint.org and Free2work.org
I-Empathize
I-empathize joined us for one day (Wednesday) to have a room with displays, audio
visual and actual artifacts from rescued sex trafficking victims. They also set up
mattresses outside where people could pay $10 to sit on one to give visuals to modern
day slavery. In addition, they had an info booth with Soularium questions.
• Set-up (how far in advance do you need to start and what needs to be done?):
Dates with I-empathize need to be set up at least 2 months in advance and rooms
confirmed; they need big rooms with 10’ ceilings, and preferably where they can
leave stuff overnight.
• Contacts (include name, contact info and location)
What went well: Plaza visuals were VERY helpful.
What didn’t/needs to be changed: Be sure to get good rooms ahead of time. I think it
would be beneficial to have I-empathize multiple days instead of just one.
Bricks on Campus
Provide a visualization of the reality of slave labor.
• Purchased 50 bricks from an ad on Craigslist for $20. I’d recommend trying to
get 5 times as many bricks (or more, 1000 would be awesome!) Maybe someone
would let us “borrow” a full pallet and we then just pay for any we break. Worth
checking into at Lowe’s, Home Depot, etc.
• We had sign-ups at FRESHMAN Bible Studies and the Justice Week info
meeting for 30 minute time slots. You need at least two people the whole time
but we had more for most of it, as many as 6 carrying bricks at once. The more
the merrier (and bigger impact)! This was good especially during passing
periods so we would be obvious. At some points we had people handing out IJM
cards with facts on them and trying to engage people in conversation (this
worked better during class times when there were fewer people walking by). It
would be cool to bring “passer-bys” into the demonstration and have them join
in carrying bricks.
• Participants carried 1-2 bricks at a time and held them on top of their heads for a
better visual. We carried bricks from east to west (and back) across the plaza
building one stack and then moving it back to the original location about 30-40
yards away and so on. This way we were crossing through everyone that walked
by. Also, it’s cool to have a couple people just stand silent in the middle of traffic
holding a stack of bricks while others are carrying bricks around them.
Participants also wore white signs that said “I am a SLAVE trapped by bonded
labor.” and had IJM.org on the bottom. The signs were on a cardboard backing
that hung by metal chains from the neck. They looked pretty cool.
• Most participants seemed to enjoy the experience and I know for a number of
students it helped them to think about what goes on and engage with those
forced into slave labor. I would recommend really encouraging participants to
think about this and put themselves in a “slaves shoes” while they are carrying
the bricks. The task is very monotonous and boring but, in part, that is the
point.
• Idea for next year: pass out bricks to a lot of students and have them carry them
in their hands all day long (to classes, lunch, etc), using the brick as a
conversation piece to engage people with the idea of justice and what we are
doing. Arm them with info cards they could give to interested people.
IJM Documentary
Show “The End of Slavery” in the student union, multiple times (every hour on the
hour). This was a one day event. I would show it from 11am-3pm or later.

Showing Taken
Showing a movie about slavery or trafficking to help raise awareness and keep
encouraging others to get involved. Also as a fun hang out time to keep promoting IJM.
• Set-up (how far in advance do you need to start and what needs to be done?):
